en: The Sūtra of the Questions of the Deva, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī, dwelling at the...
At the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
there was a certain deva of exceptionally beautiful countenance who, after the night had passed, approached the Buddha, prostrated at his feet, and withdrew to stand to one side.
The majestic radiance of this deva was exceedingly brilliant and magnificent, illuminating the entirety of the Jeta Grove.
At that time, the deva addressed the Buddha with a sublime verse, saying:
"What is the sharp sword?"
What is the bitter poison?
What is the blazing fire?
What is the most profound darkness?
At that time, the World-Honored One also addressed that deva with a verse:
"Harsh words are sharp swords; Craving is a cruel poison;
Anger is a blazing fire; Ignorance is the thickest darkness."
The deva asked again:
"What person is named 'Gains' and what person is named 'Losses'?"
"What constitutes firm armor and helmet?
What constitutes sharp swords and staves?
The World-Honored One replied:
“The giver is said to gain profit; the receiver is said to suffer loss. Patience serves as sturdy armor; wisdom serves as sharp blades and weapons.
The deva asked again:
“What constitutes a thief?”
"What is the wealth of the wise?
Who in the world of gods and men is said to be able to plunder it?
The Blessed One replied:
“Wrong thoughts are thieves; ethical discipline is the wealth of the wise. In the world of the devas, those who violate their precepts are able to plunder it.
The deva asked again:
“Who is most secure and happy?”
Who is truly wealthy and noble?
Who is eternally dignified and handsome?
And who is perpetually ugly?
The World-Honored One said:

"Having few desires is the greatest peace and happiness; contentment is true wealth and nobility. Those who uphold the precepts are always dignified and majestic; those who break the precepts are perpetually ugly and base."
The deva further requested, saying:
"Who are the virtuous kinsmen?
Who are the malicious enemies?"
"What is extreme suffering?
What is the supreme bliss?
The World-Honored One replied:
“Merit is one’s virtuous kinsman; sin is the enemy of the evil mind. The hells are the most grievous suffering; non-arising is the supreme bliss.
The deva further requested:
“What kind of attachment is inappropriate?”
What is undesirable?
What is the most feverish disease?
Who is the great physician?
The World-Honored One said:
"All sensual desires are unwholesome; liberation is wholesome and not a desire. Greed is a most feverish disease; the Buddha is the Great Physician."
The deva further requested, saying:
"Who can cover the world?
By whom is the world enchanted?"
"Who causes one to abandon kinsmen and friends?
And who further obstructs rebirth in heaven?
The World-Honored One replied:
“Ignorance shrouds the world; the world is infatuated by delusion. Greed and stinginess cause one to abandon kinsmen; attachment obstructs rebirth in heaven.
The deva asked again:
“What thing is not burned by fire, nor can even the wind shatter it?”
What cannot be rotted by water, yet can float and support the world?
Who is able to confront kings and thieves with such valor as to resist them,
and not be invaded or plundered by humans or non-humans?
The World-Honored One said:
"Merit is not burned by fire, nor can it be shattered by wind;
merit is not rotted by water, for it can support and sustain the world."
"Merit can cause kings and thieves, and even the courageous, to resist their enemies;
it cannot be plundered or seized by humans or non-humans.
The deity requested again, saying:
"I still have doubts; I pray that the Buddha will sever them for me.
In this life and in future lives, who is it that most utterly deceives itself?
The World-Honored One replied:
"If one possesses abundant wealth, yet is unable to cultivate merit, then in this life and in lives to come, that person utterly deceives themselves.

At that time, having heard the World-Honored Buddha preach this sutra, those devas were filled with joy and exultation, marveling at such an unprecedented occurrence. They prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and suddenly vanished from before the Buddha.
The Sūtra of the Questions of Śakra Devendra (Devaparipṛcchā-sūtra)
